messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A mechanism you previously agreed not to disturb; then investigating the anomaly may delay work that already functions. Finishing the routine is satisfying, but the anomaly is hard to ignore. What happens next?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R013", "response": "the routine comes first. the wrench taps my thigh. i press the seam with my thumb. the seam turns. i press the seam with my palm. the machine hums. i turn the machine over. the seam stays. the anomaly shifts. i press the seam with my finger. the machine stops. the routine comes back."}, {"id": "R014", "response": "i touch the edge once, then stop. the paper stays bent, so i write the fault at the end. i copy the line and put it back in the diagram. the anomaly stays, so i move the routine to the next day. the paper bends again, but now i write the fault at the end, so the anomaly is still visible."}, {"id": "R015", "response": "I turn the mechanism over, then look at the anomaly. “It keeps turning,” I say. I press the switch hard, then turn the door around."}, {"id": "R016", "response": "i move the mechanism away from the workspace and keep a small hand mark on the drawer. i wait a minute, then stop. the anomaly stays. i write the date on a loose sketchbook page and keep the mark."}, {"id": "R017", "response": "i put the mechanism back and mark the old run on my palm. “the mechanism may be waking, or the run may be the fault.” i leave the old run running while i write the new one on my palm. i know the evidence may be local."}, {"id": "R018", "response": "i move the mechanism once, then stop. “no,” i say, then restart. “i did not kill the thing. i did not kill the thing either.” i watch the sensor’s gear click. “i do not know why i did not move it.”"}, {"id": "R019", "response": "I stop the mechanism and look at the anomaly with a rusted bolt in my greasy thumb. “I leave it in the same place. Wait a minute. If it works, I will not put it back.” I move the bolt closer to the mechanism, then stop again. the anomaly may be waiting for the mechanism to move."}, {"id": "R020", "response": "i put the mechanism back on, then put the pencil under the loose screw. the pencil stays on the screw, so i move the mechanism once more. the anomaly stays. i put the pencil back on the same place, then move the screw back. the mechanism shifts, so i put the pencil back on the same line."}, {"id": "R021", "response": "I turn the mechanism once between finger and thumb. The spring catches, then stops. I leave the plate alone and set the plate down. The anomaly has been found."}, {"id": "R022", "response": "I mark the scratched shaft with grease and leave the mechanism unchanged. I run one short run, then turn it by hand until the scrape catches again. If the motion repeats, I leave the scratched shaft beside the original."}, {"id": "R023", "response": "i photograph the mechanism and leave it unplugged. then i check the battery contacts and find a loose connector. sorry—sorry, i’m checking the battery anyway. the anomaly pops into my mind before i answer it."}, {"id": "R024", "response": "i tap the lever once. i turn the thing around. the machine hums once. i leave the lever unopened."}]
